method: Read all five incoming bodies and editorial notes in seed-context.packet.json in full, and all eleven included Darwin-to-Kemp witness bodies in full. Compared distinctive botanical, paper, and testimonial content without treating these incoming texts as direct prompts for the Kemp letters. Preserved held XML date bounds and separated dated Darwin attestations from physical seed/specimen events.

proposed_links.reason: Darwin's 24 April response repeats Lindley's two seed identifications and expectation of common species. The incoming 669 is held as [after 8 Apr 1843], so the link establishes knowledge by 24 April without narrowing the source's raw bound.

exact_quotes.quote: one is certainly a Polygonum, and the other in all probability a Chenopodium
one of the seeds is certainly a Polygonum & the other probably a Chenopodium

proposed_links.reason: Darwin's 8 September letter repeats Lindley's identification of Rumex acetosella and an unknown Atriplex, and Lindley's uncertainty about Atriplex patula. The source is bounded [before 2 Sept 1843]; the response date supplies a latest knowledge-by date only.

exact_quotes.quote: Your Scotch seeds proved Rumex Acetosella & this Atriplex
turn out to be Rumex acetosella & an Atriplex, which Lindley does not know

proposed_links.reason: Henslow's 9 October botanical conclusion that Kemp's Atriplex is clearly A. patula is explicitly relayed by Darwin in 705F, which says he has heard from Henslow and repeats the same conclusion. This is cross-correspondent knowledge, not a direct Kemp prompt.

exact_quotes.quote: the supposed A. hastata will turn out after all to be only a strange var. of Atriplex patula a very common plant
Prof. Henslow, now suspects that the Atriplex is merely a variety of the common A. patula

proposed_links.reason: Henslow's 17 October letter supplies the A. patula conclusion and distinguishes Lindley's odd Atriplex from Kemp's specimen; Darwin's 1 November witness incorporates Henslow's A. patula conclusion into his publication assessment.

exact_quotes.quote: Mr K’s was clearly only A. patula, & this it is that staggers me
the Atriplex reared by you is undoubtedly according to Henslow the A. patula

proposed_links.reason: Babington's 26 October incoming letter identifies the Hort. Society plant as A. angustifolia and says Kemp's specimen should be compared with Henslow's A. patula; Darwin's 1 November witness reports Babington's determination and encloses his letter.

exact_quotes.quote: a variety of the A. angustifolia
Mr Babington (who from the te⁠⟨⁠s⁠⟩⁠timony of several Botanists, is a first-rate judge in the genus Atriplex) pronounces the plant reared at the Hort. Soc. to be A. angustifolium

candidate_links.reason: The same-day Henslow letter and Darwin's 701F concern the same Atriplex inquiry, but 701F says Darwin will write Henslow to urge completion, so it does not securely establish that 701 was already received and read before 701F.

exact_quotes.quote: His other two are equally common
I will write by today’s post to urge him to complete his examination.

issues.finding: The incoming XML bound is held as [after 8 Apr 1843] with an open upper possibility extending to 1882; 672F dated 24 April establishes Darwin's knowledge by that date but does not rewrite the raw incoming constraint.

evidence.quote: I have heard from Prof. Lindley

issues.finding: The incoming XML bound is [before 2 Sept 1843]; 691F on 8 September establishes a knowledge-by date but does not identify an exact delivery or reading day for 690.

evidence.quote: The seeds you sent me from the sand-pit

issues.finding: Seed, specimen, paper, and enclosed-letter references are kept distinct from incoming-letter receipt. The witnesses establish quoted or relayed information and, where stated, receipt of papers or letters, but do not turn every physical specimen event into a dated incoming text.

evidence.quote: your paper has reached me safely

limitations: These links are cross-correspondent knowledge relations into Darwin's Kemp-facing witnesses. They are not direct replies to Kemp letters and do not assert that Darwin read the incoming source on its XML date.
